The order applies to property acquired under orders placed after August 15, 1971 and before December 20, 1971, a window that closed before the order was signed on April 11, 1972, and clause (b) calls for lists of items to be published from time to time by the Secretary of the Treasury. An end date and the relation of the window to 26 U.S.C. 48(a)(7) cannot be supported without the held text of that statute and of the Treasury lists; missing sources: section 48(a)(7) as then in force and the published item lists.

The order sets staggered two-year terms for Indian-leader members of the National Council on Indian Opportunity, a clause that runs while the Council exists. No held source ends the Council (EO 11399 and EO 11551 are held and contain no termination provision, and no ending instrument is held), and the dossier lists a census gap for PL:91-125. Missing source: the instrument or statute that terminated the Council, or a held text of the Council's last appointments.

The order sets interest equalization tax rates at zero under section 4911(b)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 by rewriting section 1 of EO 11464; the tax's end rests on a statute (the dossier flags PL:94-455 as absent from the census) whose text is not held, and EO 11754, the order it follows, is held only as actor context with no located provision. Missing sources: the statute that ended or repealed section 4911 and the text of EO 11464 as amended.

The order amends section 2 of EO 11692 to read 'This order shall take effect October 1, 1972', and the dossier's clause inventory is wrong: its seven clauses are text from neighbouring Cost of Living Council rules on the same Federal Register pages, so an inventory correction is needed. The end of the amended section depends on EO 11812 (signed October 7, 1974, effective October 1, 1974), whose provision is held, but whether an amendment of an effective-date sentence continues until its parent ends or was spent on signing, and which date applies given the retroactive effective date, is not resolved from held evidence.

The order authorizes the House Judiciary Committee to inspect President Nixon's tax returns in connection with House Resolution 803, with no stated end; no held source shows when the authority was exhausted or ended (no committee report, resolution text or later order is held). Missing source: a held record of when the impeachment inquiry's access ended, or a revoking instrument.
